title: Web UI render + weak/strong badges
goal: Read-only tree viewer renders composed project data with clear weak/strong visual signals for session orient.
out: editing node status in the UI

claims.text: Loads project list into a dropdown and fetches `/api/tree/<project>` to render the composed `nodes` tree recursively
`status: weak` nodes show a rose badge (`.badge-status-weak`) AND a pink row highlight with left accent (`data-status="weak"`, `.node-weak`)
claims.rationale: Weak nodes must pop for pick-weak orient

claims.text: `status: strong` nodes show a teal badge (`.badge-status-strong` in styles.css)
claims.rationale: Trusted areas visually distinct from weak

claims.text: Workflow statuses (`spec_ready`, `spec_approved`, `done`, `discussing`, etc.) each map to a distinct badge color class derived from `badge-status-<status>`
claims.rationale: Status model readable at a glance

claims.text: Stale nodes show a `stale` badge and amber row background (`.node.stale > .node-row`)
Clicking a parent row toggles child visibility (▼/▶) via `.children.collapsed`
Refresh button and project dropdown re-fetch and re-render the tree; URL updates to `?project=<name>`
Root `constraints` render as chips below the header
When API returns `pending: true`, the pending banner is shown (`#pending-banner`); hidden otherwise
claims.rationale: User knows CLI approval is blocking the view

claims.text: API `compose_error` (if present) appears in the meta line under the project title
claims.rationale: Broken fragment links surface in UI

claims.text: Node `data` fields render as inline tags; tree text is HTML-escaped before insertion (no raw innerHTML from yaml strings)
claims.rationale: Safe rendering of user-authored tree content

claims.text: The viewer exposes no controls to edit tree structure or node status — read-only orient surface only
